title: Looks like a winner but is it a winner?
author: EaZyRecipeZ

comments.author: AutoBudAlpha
comments.body:
Can you give a little more info on how this works? 

Best way to know how well it works is to try it live. Also slippage destroys most of my backtest ways, but if you are only trading once per day this won’t be a huge problem

replies.author: EaZyRecipeZ
replies.body:
four independent strategies each control 25% of capital, and the bot merges their target weights into one net portfolio. Daily bars are emitted at market close, and the orders it submits are Market On Open orders, so changes are decided from todays close based signals and executed at the next market open. 

Core idea

The bot runs four models in parallel: T10, T11, S2, and S3, each returning a small weight map like “25% TQQQ” or “12.5% SQQQ + 12.5% TLT.” It then sums overlapping picks, so if two models both want TQQQ, the final target in TQQQ gets larger.

Signals

Most logic is regime based: RSI thresholds detect overbought or dip-buy setups, while 20/200-day and 202-day SMAs decide bull vs bear conditions. Warm-up is set to 215 daily bars so indicators are ready before trading, and LEAN does not allow trading during warm-up.

replies.author: AutoBudAlpha
replies.body:
Oh I like this logic! I just ran this logic against my back tester (I spent some time building this thing and it has destroyed most of my strats) it doesn’t beat buying and holding TQQQ on the last two year horizon but it definitely holds up and wins in longer cycles. 

I’m going to mess with this a bit and post some ideas for next steps if I have any. 

About me: I have been passively trading for the last 10 years (mostly safe ETFs). I have also been doing machine learning / AI for the same amount of time, but never linked them up. I’m interested in working with a group of people to build some good Strats!

comments.author: Obviously_not_maayan
comments.body: You have to include slippage, especially if your strategy is relying on getting the first second the market open..

replies.author: EaZyRecipeZ
replies.body: For this bot it doesn't care about slippage.  It only balances the stocks once a day and it doesn't have loss stop.  The stock can even drop or raise 10% it'll do the same thing.

replies.author: Obviously_not_maayan
replies.body: What do you mean doesn't care? Slippage happens everytime you buy or sell

replies.author: EaZyRecipeZ
replies.body: because it only balances the stocks.  It doesn't decide on today's price.  It decides on yesterday price.

replies.author: Obviously_not_maayan
replies.body: So you are trying to fill your orders with yesterdays price?

replies.author: EaZyRecipeZ
replies.body: no, current price of course.  Deciding factor weather to buy or sell is on daily price only.  Read my post below how the script works

replies.author: Obviously_not_maayan
replies.body: Ok whenever you are buying or selling, you are dealing with slippage

replies.author: EaZyRecipeZ
replies.body: yes, that's true but it won't effect the bot that much.

replies.author: EaZyRecipeZ
replies.body: since it's trading ETF such as TQQQ, SOXL  and etc, they are plus / minus 0.10 cents

replies.author: Obviously_not_maayan
replies.body: So if you have slippage estimation why not include it in the backtest?

replies.author: EaZyRecipeZ
replies.body: Not at the moment.  I used quantconnect backdata and I don't know if they have slippage or not but the backtest was almost identical.  I'm using yahoo backdata which doesn't have slippage but my script can include the slippage.

replies.author: EaZyRecipeZ
replies.body: I use schwab and they don't charge fee's.  The only fees that I have to pay are mandated SEC ETF fees.
